openalex.title: Matrix Factorization Techniques for Recommender Systems
openalex.abstract: As the Netflix Prize competition has demonstrated, matrix factorization models are superior to classic nearest neighbor techniques for producing product recommendations, allowing the incorporation of additional information such as implicit feedback, temporal effects, and confidence levels.

Collaborative filtering (CF) predicts user preferences by analyzing patterns in past user-item interactions, offering strong personalization but facing challenges such as cold-start problems and scalability in large urban datasets (Sarwar et al. 2001; Koren et al. 2009; Zhang et al. 2019).
For example, integrating CF with latent factor and neighborhood models reduces error rates in sparse datasets (Koren et al. 2009).

Their work highlighted that while Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is easy to implement, ALS is often more favorable for parallelization and handling implicit feedback datasets.
The primary advantage of ALS in our high-dimensional context is its amenability to parallelization.

We implement a highly optimized Alternating Least Squares (ALS) framework, accelerated via Just-In-Time (JIT) compilation, to decompose the interaction matrix into lower-dimensional user and item embeddings.
This confirms that the ALS algo-rithm recovered meaningful latent structures solely from interaction data, without access to metadata tags.
Rather than retraining the full model, we calculated the user’s latent vector using a single iteration of the ALS user step, keeping all item parameters fixed.
